title: Release gates
point: A change moves from offline eval to shadow to canary to full rollout. Safety failures block absolutely, quality blocks only on significant regressions, and cost is reported beside quality.
definition: Release gates are the checks a prompt, model or tool change must pass at each rollout stage. Safety assertions block on any failure, quality regressions block when statistically significant, and guardrail metrics trigger automatic rollback.

objective.text: Given a proposed prompt change, define the gates for offline eval, shadow, canary and full rollout, including the significance test and rollback triggers.

misconceptions.claim: Any drop in the average golden-set score should block the release.
misconceptions.correction: Small drops are often noise. Block a quality regression only when a paired test on per-item scores, such as a sign test or bootstrap, shows it is significant.

misconceptions.claim: A quality gain is always worth shipping.
misconceptions.correction: Report cost next to quality. A two-point gain that triples spend per conversation is a business trade, and it should be a visible decision, not a side effect.

l1: Offline eval scores the change on the golden set before any user sees it. Shadow mode then runs it on live traffic without showing its answers.
A canary serves a small share of real users, such as 5 per cent, while guardrail metrics are watched. Full rollout follows only if the canary holds.
Safety assertions, such as never revealing another customer's data, block on any failure. Quality and cost are compared with the current version.
l2: Take a 300-item golden set. The new prompt beats the old on 41 items, loses on 29 and ties on 230. Only the 70 items that differ count in a sign test.
With no real change, wins among 70 would average 35 with a standard deviation of about 4.2. A count of 41 is about 1.4 deviations above, so the gain is not significant.
The release can still ship as neutral, but the report must not claim an improvement. If a safety assertion had failed even once, the release would be blocked whatever the score.
l3: Set canary rollback triggers in advance, such as escalation rate up 3 points or p95 latency above 12 seconds over an hour. Rollback is then automatic, not a meeting.
A canary must be large enough to see the effect. At 5 per cent of 200,000 conversations a month, about 330 canary conversations a day can resolve only fairly large changes.
Report cost per conversation beside quality for every candidate. A change that raises quality 2 points and cost from $0.02 to $0.06 then reaches the decision as an explicit trade.
